commits.message:
fix(columns): a declared column width yields to a narrower offer (rich-table-width-y1a)

`new Columns(items, { width: 6 })` rendered at `maxWidth: 3` laid out one
six-cell column and emitted six-cell lines into a three-cell request, while
`measure` already reported three. The terminal soft-wraps an oversized line and
the wrap takes the frame of everything printed after it.

`Columns._declaredWidth(options)` bounds the declared width by the offer, and
both `_divide` (render) and `_naturalWidth` (measure) read it, the same shape
`Table._outerWidth` gave the Table half of this ticket in #79. A declared width
is now what a column asks for, not what it takes, across both renderables.

The width sweep gains "Columns at a declared width" and "Columns at a declared
unbounded width", and the header note that excluded declared-width Columns is
deleted. Without the fix those two configurations and the new pinned test in
columns.test.ts fail (5 tests); with it the suite is green.

docs/tables.md said a declared `width` was a "Fixed total width — disables
auto-sizing, and overrides a container narrower than it". Neither half is true
on master: the container wins, and a declared width is a ceiling the table sizes
to its content within — five cells of content under `width: 40` render at five
unless `expand` is set (verified unchanged back to before #77). "Narrow widths"
now states that contract once, and the Sizing row links to it.
docs/columns.md gains the `width` row it never had.

Filed, not fixed here: rich-columns-awe (Columns `expand` and `padding` are
accepted and never applied) and rich-table-width-5cj (whether a declared Table
width should imply `expand`, as it does in upstream Rich).

fix(traceback): drop options the renderer ignores and document real output (rich-traceback-i5d) (#142)

* fix(traceback): drop options the renderer ignores and document real output (rich-traceback-i5d)

TracebackOptions accepted showLocals, width and theme and read none of
them, and docs/traceback.md showed a bordered panel with highlighted
source lines and a locals table that the renderer has never produced.

Locals are removed rather than implemented. An Error records where each
frame was, not what was in scope; the only node route to that is an
inspector session pausing on exceptions, which would have to pause on
every throw, caught ones included, to serve new Traceback(caughtError),
and which a browser cannot run at all. width and theme sized and
coloured the source excerpt that does not exist either.

docs/traceback.md, the docs index card and the README blurb now show
the output as rendered. The suppress example passed a module object to
a string[] option and now passes a string.

Pinning the maxFrames sample turned up a truncation bug: slice(-half)
is the whole array when maxFrames is 1, and an odd budget showed one
frame fewer than it counted. The tail now takes maxFrames - head frames
from an index, so the budget is spent exactly.

* docs(traceback): capture the max-frames sample from a real stack (rich-traceback-i5d)

The previous sample came from a hand-written 250-frame error.stack. V8
records Error.stackTraceLimit frames, 10 by default, so no real error
reaches the default cap of 100 and the sample could not be reproduced.
The section now says to raise the limit, and the sample is output
captured from a real recursion under plain node.

The sample's last two frames show the async marker read as part of
the function name, filed as rich-traceback-dbs.
